name: specify-a-feature
when_to_use: When the user needs a concrete feature plan.
When the flow must gather context and drive implementation.

steps.description: Capture the feature goal and success criteria.
steps.details: Ask about outcomes, edge cases, tests, and constraints.

steps.description: Generate the system template and fill it out.
steps.details: Fill the system template before review.

steps.description: Review the system context before deciding the feature shape.
steps.details: Confirm requirements, approach, and constraints after fill.

steps.description: Generate the architecture template and fill it out.
steps.details: Capture the entity model before review.

steps.description: Review architecture before implementation.
steps.details: Confirm model, relationships, invariants, and guidance after fill.

steps.description: Generate the implementation template and fill it out.
steps.details: Complete the template with decisions and reasoning.

steps.description: Decide on proposed PRs and fill each template.
steps.details: Fill PR templates with intent, criteria, tests, and risks.

steps.description: Prompt the user to review the result.
steps.details: Show the draft plan and confirm it still matches.

steps.description: Incorporate the user's approved feedback into the feature plan.
steps.details: Update the specifications and proposed PRs only when the user confirms a change.

steps.description: Validate every generated specification before implementation.
steps.details: Run every validation command below in order. If any command fails, fix the reported issue and restart this validation step; advance only when all four documents agree.

steps.description: If any specification validation fails, fix it and return to the validation step.
steps.details: Do not begin implementation or create a pull request while any required specification remains invalid.

steps.description: Prepare an implementation checklist from each approved proposed PR.
steps.details: For every proposed PR, identify the code files, tests, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and validation commands before making changes. Keep each item traceable to the approved specifications.

steps.description: Implement the approved feature changes and their tests.
steps.details: Keep the specifications and implementation aligned as the code changes are made.

steps.description: Run local formatting, linting, type checks, and tests.
steps.details: Fix local failures before creating or updating the pull request.

steps.description: Create or update the pull request for the validated feature.
steps.details: Create the draft pull request from the feature branch with the feature intent, implementation scope, validation evidence, and remaining risks. If a pull request already exists for the branch, update it instead.

steps.description: Wait 30 seconds for CI to make progress.
steps.details: This is the first checkpoint in the CI monitoring loop.

steps.description: If CI has finished, check its result.
steps.details: Inspect all required checks for the pull request before deciding whether the loop can exit.

steps.description: If CI passed, break out of the CI monitoring loop.
steps.details: Record the successful checks and continue to the final user handoff.

steps.description: If CI failed, fix the reported failures and return to the wait step.
steps.details: Apply only fixes supported by the failure evidence, rerun local validation, and keep the pull request updated.

steps.description: If CI is still running, return to the wait step.
steps.details: Do not treat pending checks as a failure or as completion.

steps.description: Prompt the user to review the implementation and CI result.
steps.details: Show the final pull request, validation evidence, and CI outcome for approval.
